detail.overview:
Can you turn satellite imagery into accurate road networks for underserved communities?

Accurate road maps are the foundation for disaster response, access to health services, infrastructure planning and community development. Yet in many low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), roads are missing or out of date on OpenStreetMap and similar tools. A 2023 study found that road mapping was still in its early stages in 10.5% of assessed urban centers in South Asia and 5.9% in Sub-Saharan Africa. Tracing roads by hand from imagery is slow, so the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOTOSM) built its fAIr tool to speed this up with AI models.

In this challenge, your objective is to build a machine learning model that detects roads in high-resolution satellite and aerial image tiles. Your model will be scored on imagery from regions and sources that are not in the training data, where roads, surfaces, vegetation and image quality all differ, so it must generalise rather than memorise. You may use external data or pretrained models, provided you disclose the source.

Your solution will give volunteer mappers a first draft of the roads to review and correct, instead of tracing them from scratch, and winning methods will inform the models used in fAIr. Better road maps help responders plan routes and health programmes reach communities, particularly in LMICs where mapping gaps are largest. Because the training data and winning models will be openly licensed, other mapping organisations can also reuse the methods.

Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT)
The Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) is an international nonprofit organization dedicated to improving lives through open geographic data, community-driven mapping, and innovative geospatial technologies. HOT collaborates with local communities, volunteers, humanitarian organizations, and development partners to create accessible, high-quality maps, particularly in underserved and vulnerable regions. Its work supports disaster response, climate resilience, sustainable development, and informed decision-making while empowering communities to build local mapping capacity.
As part of its mission, HOT developed fAIr, an open-source, AI-assisted mapping platform that enables communities to train, customize, and deploy localized computer vision models to identify geographic features, such as buildings and roads, from high-resolution aerial and drone imagery. By combining artificial intelligence with local knowledge and human validation, fAIr accelerates geospatial data creation, strengthens community-driven mapping, and makes GeoAI technologies more accessible for humanitarian and development applications worldwide.
detail.evaluation:
This challenge uses three metrics to assess how closely your predicted centrelines follow the reference roads and how well they preserve connections. The leaderboard score uses multimetric evaluation - a weighted average of the three metrics. Scores range from 0 to 1, with higher scores being better. If two submissions receive the same score, the earlier submission ranks higher.

Buffered Centreline F1 (micro), 50%. Precision is the proportion of predicted centreline pixels within 1 metre of a reference centreline. Recall is the proportion of reference centreline pixels within 1 metre of a predicted centreline. Pixel counts are pooled across the evaluation split before F1 is calculated.

Average Path Length Similarity (APLS), 30%. Compares shortest path lengths in the predicted and reference road networks within each tile. Missing routes and differences in path length lower the score. Scores are averaged across tiles where APLS can be calculated.

TOPO F1, 20%. Compares the parts of the local road network reachable from corresponding points in the predicted and reference networks. It measures whether the prediction preserves nearby branches and connections.

Ties are broken by the earlier submission time.

Submission format
Use SampleSubmission.csv as your template. Keep the columns ID, geometry and metres_per_pixel in the order shown. Submit one row per test tile and leave metres_per_pixel blank. The scorer uses the pixel scale for each tile from the reference files.

Enter your predicted road centrelines as a two-dimensional Well-Known Text (WKT) MULTILINESTRING, even if you predict a single line. Use the original tile’s pixel coordinates, with (0, 0) at the top-left corner, x increasing to the right and y increasing downwards.…
detail.data_or_tools:
The training set contains 7,246 labelled aerial image tiles from Freetown, Sierra Leone; Nairobi, Kenya; and Stellenbosch, South Africa. Train.csv contains the OpenStreetMap road centrelines and pixel scale for each tile. Some training tiles contain no mapped roads. The test set contains 4,548 tiles.

External datasets
SpaceNet 3 Roads and SROADEX are external sources you can use in line with the challenge rules. If you use external data or pretrained models, disclose their sources.

- 
SpaceNet 3 Roads: Satellite imagery (0.3m), covering Las Vegas, Paris, Shanghai, Khartoum. Tiles are 1,300 × 1,300px (about 400 × 400m) and include GeoJSON centrelines covering over 8,000 km of mapped roads. Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0.

- 
SROADEX (Train and Evaluation Code): Aerial orthophotos (0.5m), covering Spain. Tiles are 256 × 256px (about 128m across). The dataset includes 250,442 tiles with binary road masks and 276,715 images without roads. Licence: CC BY 4.0.

Test imagery
Test images are supplied as 256 × 256 pixel, 8-bit RGB PNGs without georeferencing. The ID in Test.csv matches the image filename without the .png extension.…
detail.eligibility:
Languages and tools: You may only use open-source languages and tools in building models for this challenge.
Who can compete: Open to all
This challenge is open to all.
Datasets, packages and general principles
The solution must use publicly-available, open-source packages only.
Note that to count, your submission must first pass processing. If your submission fails during the processing step, it will not be counted and not receive a score; nor will it count against your daily submission limit. If you encounter problems with your submission file, your best course of action is to ask for advice on the challenge page.
The winners will be paid via bank transfer, PayPal if payment is less than or equivalent to $100, or other international money transfer platform. International transfer fees will be deducted from the total prize amount, unless the prize money is under $500, in which case the international transfer fees will be covered by Zindi. In all cases, the winners are responsible for any other fees applied by their own bank or other institution for receiving the prize money. All taxes imposed on prizes are the sole responsibility of the winners.…

Individual entry
Team size: Max team size of 4
Code sharing: Multiple accounts, or sharing of code and information across accounts not in teams, is not allowed and will lead to disqualification.
detail.submission:
Submission Limits: 3 submissions per day, 80 submissions overall.
Public-Private Split: Zindi maintains a public leaderboard and a private leaderboard for each challenge. The Public Leaderboard includes approximately 28% of the test dataset. The private leaderboard will be revealed at the close of the challenge and contains the remaining 72% of the test set.
Code Review: Top 10 on the private leaderboard will receive an email requesting their code at the close of the challenge. You will have 48 hours to submit your code.
You may participate in challenges as an individual or in a team of up to four people. When creating a team, the team must have a total submission count less than or equal to the maximum allowable submissions as of the formation date. A team will be allowed the maximum number of submissions for the challenge, minus the total number of submissions among team members at team formation. Prizes are transferred only to the individual players or to the team leader.
Multiple accounts per user are not permitted, and neither is collaboration or membership across multiple teams. Individuals and their submissions originating from multiple accounts will be immediately disqualified from the platform.
